title: Habibsters: The League's First Dynasty, Still Waiting on the Third Ring
body: Every league needs a standard, and in the Buckaroo Football League that standard has always been Kaushal. Habib walked into the inaugural 2023 season, went 10-4, grabbed the No. 1 seed with 1,528.8 points, and lifted Buckaroo Bowl I like he had rehearsed it. Even his lowest moment that year, a 74.5-point dud against Sonny in week 9, came during a title run, which is the kind of bad week most managers would frame and hang on the wall.

Then he did it again. The 2024 Habibsters went 11-3, took the top seed for a second straight year with 1,524.8 points, and won Buckaroo Bowl II. Habibi also doubled his waiver activity, from 16 pickups to 32, proving a two-time champ can still work the wire like a walk-on fighting for a roster spot. For a UGA guy who lives for college football, back-to-back titles must have felt like home.

The 2025 season was the plot twist. The Habibsters scored a career-high 1,973.6 points and posted his best week ever, a 151.5-point demolition of Ramon in week 2, yet still finished 8-8. He snuck in as the No. 3 seed, took his first-ever playoff loss, and finished third. His playoff record is still a sparkling 4-1, but that season started the bad-luck chapter of the Kaushal story, where the points show up and the wins don't.

The head-to-head ledger shows who Habib has owned. He is 9-2 against Mekhi, 8-4 against Ramon, and 7-2 against Alan, which makes him something of a hero in this league. The one real thorn is Randy, the only longtime rival who holds a winning record over him at 6-5, while the series with Sonny is a coin-flip 6-5 in Kaushal's favor. Zoe is 1-0 against him in her rookie year, a fact she is surely bringing up at every opportunity.

Here is the strangest stat in his file: zero trades, ever, across four seasons. Kaushal builds through the draft and the waiver wire (20 pickups already in 2026) and apparently hasn't hit the trade button since the league began. That approach has him at 3-4 with 797.8 points and 15% title odds right now, outside the playoff picture but well within range. This is a man who once got pulled over speeding in Georgia, so nobody should be surprised if he comes flying back up the standings.
